structured.answer: Yes, it's worth having. My boss puts in money on top of my salary that only goes into this fund, and after 6 years from the first deposit I can take everything out with no tax. Before that I can still take it, but it gets taxed. The example showed about 14,000 ₪ in tax on a 5‑year withdrawal.

stuck.why: The example is set to withdrawing at 5 years, so the first scary thing I see is a red −13,974 ₪ 'המס'. For a second I thought the fund costs that much, until I saw the small bars marked 'לפני 6 שנים: מס' and 'מ־6 שנים: פטור ממס'.
Too many numbers in one block. I couldn't tell if it applies to me, so I skipped it.

used: 'אחרי 6 שנים מההפקדה הראשונה אפשר למשוך... בלי מס'
'אפשר למשוך גם לפני 6 השנים, אבל אז משלמים'

Small bars labelled 'לפני 6 שנים: מס' / 'מ־6 שנים: פטור ממס'

unsure_meaning: Whether the 2% management fee is a lot. It just sounds small.
What the teal vs yellow vs grey parts of the bars mean (I guessed teal = profit, yellow = boss's money)
not_found: Which company or track I'm actually in, and how to check
A plain 'what to do first' step for someone whose employer already signed them up
The fee in shekels instead of percent

findings.what: The example is set to withdrawing at 5 years, so the biggest scary number is a red −13,974 ₪ tax. That makes the fund look bad at first glance, when the main point is that it's tax-free after 6.
Management fee is only shown as 'עד 2%', with no shekel amount, so I can't tell if it matters
Dense block of ceilings and percentages (7.5%, 2.5%, 15,712 ₪, 20,566 ₪) right at the top, hard to read on a phone
Lots of jargon (מס רווחי הון, הרווח הריאלי, הפקדה מוטבת) with no plain-words version
Chart colours aren't explained next to the bars
